newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli bonds end higher, CPI-linked bonds rise.
newsitem.headline: Israeli bonds end higher, CPI-linked bonds rise.

text.p: Israeli bond prices closed higher in moderate on Sunday as bonds linked to the consumer price index (CPI) posted strong gains, traders said.
* Unlinked government bonds (Gilon - issued for four years): +0.09 pct to 169.01.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.08 pct at 159.86
Volume was moderate at 152 million shekels with all bonds rising except the dollar-linked bonds, traders said.

"Long inflation-linked bonds rose today. The provident funds are generating high demand for these bonds, but activity is very low. The funds are simply trying to improve their results before the end of the year," said Danni Scharia at Capital Securities.

"Demand for the CPI-linked bonds was around 180 million shekels against supply of only 18 million shekels. Total turnover was only 26 million shekels. Because of the relatively low volume the long, linked bonds posted nice gains today," said Shlomit Hacker at Israel Discount Bank.

"Unlinked bonds continue to rise because the economic slowdown is evident. Despite expectations for a relatively high October CPI, of around 0.9 percent, the unlinked bonds continue to be very attractive," Scharia added.
The Central Bureau of Statistics will announce October's CPI on November 15.

Makams (which are also unlinked) posted slight gains. Traders noted that the Makams usually rise on Sunday, after two days when there is no trading. Activity in the Makams was low with turnover at only 49 million shekels.
"Dollar linked bonds posted slight losses but activity was very low with volume of only nine million shekels. Most issues closed unchanged," Hacker said.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
